prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-finished character design.
Image 1 is the USER'S ROUGH PAINTOVER DESIGN DIRECTION. It is a schematic, not finished art to trace literally. Interpret its intentional silhouette and pose changes, then redraw the ENTIRE character cleanly with coherent anatomy and cloth construction. Remove ALL rough scribbles, overpaint seams, erased patches, leftover obsolete hands, incomplete legs and background marks.
Image 2 is ONLY the clean character identity, gentle youthful face, silver hair, modest Chinese clothing and established painting base. Its old horn shape and stiff pose are superseded by image 1.
Image 3 is the project's gem-icon painting authority: strong ink contour, few large coherent purple light/shadow planes, matte hand-painted clarity, no smooth airbrushed anime gradients and no tiny mosaic shards.

Follow these user-drawn changes faithfully:
1. HEAD: replace the bulky upright demon-like horns with TWO slender elegant dark-purple BUTTERFLY ANTENNA-LIKE HEAD ORNAMENTS, sweeping upward and BACK toward screen-right in long graceful curves. Each ends in a flattened tapered violet leaf/club tip, like the paintover. Both are attached coherently to a minimal dark hairband/forehead ornament, not floating strokes. Keep silver-white hair, pointed elf ears, soft young rounded face and kind lavender eyes. Do not retain the old thick horn base behind the new antennas.
2. MAGIC HAND / TALISMANS: raise one forearm in front of her toward screen-left, elbow bent and palm gently UP at about shoulder/chin height, as painted. EXACTLY THREE warm-ivory rectangular Chinese paper talismans float in a small loose fan above this palm. Each has ONE simple bold violet abstract talisman seal, not words or copied scribble artifacts. Small variation in tilt, all three separate and readable. No extra cards, no floating butterfly and no huge glowing effects.
3. CORRECT TWO-ARM ANATOMY: raised hand must connect through wrist, forearm, elbow and sleeve to its shoulder. This raised arm REPLACES the obsolete hand holding the collar visible underneath the user's overpaint. There are EXACTLY TWO arms and TWO hands in the final: the raised palm and the other small relaxed hand near waist. REMOVE the old third chest/clasp hand. The raised sleeve has an ivory lining exposed in a broad hanging triangular fold beneath the forearm, connected correctly at the wrist and shoulder.
4. CLOAK: preserve the very LARGE PURPLE BUTTERFLY CLOAK, narrow at shoulders and broadly triangular below, but make its spread diagonally asymmetrical like the paintover: a wide outward near panel toward screen-right, narrower far panel sweeping down-left. It is one shoulder-attached CLOTH cloak, not rigid insect wings or duplicated wing sleeves. Large angular-curved upper/lower wing lobes, deliberate notch and long tapered corners. One large lavender/cyan butterfly wing-eye mark on each side, following clear large lit/turned cloth planes. The body remains readable through the front opening.
5. DISTINCTIVE LONG BUTTERFLY TAILS: extend the cloak's LOWER CORNERS into TWO dark-purple slender yet substantial sweeping SWALLOWTAIL BUTTERFLY extensions. Their curves trail down and outward as in the sketch, then end in broadened teardrop/leaf-shaped tips with a SIMPLE pale-cyan and violet eye mark. They are continuous cloth extensions, not detached tassels, extra limbs or loose scribbles. Two elegant long curves only, clearly separated from legs and background, avoid spaghetti. Retain the big triangular cape mass above them.
6. POSE: capture the user's light asymmetrical step/weight shift, organically correcting the rough painted legs. Whole figure is front three-quarter SCREEN LEFT, with face, sternum, pelvis and knees agreeing. One leg supports the body; the other bends softly and steps a little forward-left, creating gentle motion and a narrow gap between two visible boots. No crossed/merged legs, backwards hips, dislocated knees, floating feet or implausible twist. Both boots correctly attached to ankles, relaxed posture, no wide squat. The cloak and long tails follow the pose direction.

Preserve the clearly YOUTHFUL chibi identity and wholesome presentation, compact approximately 3.5 head proportions excluding antenna extensions. Fully covered modest ivory-and-violet Chinese cross-collar tunic and layered skirt/tabard, opaque dark-purple leggings, simple low cloth boots. Skin only on face/ears/hands; the white painted gaps in the sketch are editing/layout marks, NOT exposed-body cutouts. No adult body sculpting or sexualized pose.
Costume has a simple narrow purple sash and small plain pale-jade clasp, modest cloud shoulder and minimal dull gold edging. Quiet large cloth shapes, do not add ornaments everywhere. Back hair gathered into a few broad silver locks within the cape silhouette. Expression warm and gently focused on the floating talismans.
Polished GAME GEM-ICON character rendering: confident clean deep-violet contour, 2–3 large matte shadow/light groups per material, controlled saturated purple and ivory, broad spare hand-painted planes. No overly fine hatching, dense facets, realistic eyes, glossy crystal surfaces, scratchy sketch edges, rough user-painted fingers, extra leftover hands or erased marks.
Output ONE completely finished full-body image on square plain uniform warm ivory. Fit antenna tips, all THREE talismans, the whole cloak, BOTH complete long butterfly tails and BOTH boots with safe margins. No title, labels, framing, comparison sheet, floor shadow or scenery.
purpose: Finish the user's schematic paintover: swept butterfly antennas, raised palm with three talismans, diagonal triangular cloak, two long swallowtail extensions and coherent gentle pose.
visual_review: Swept slender head ornaments, three floating talismans and a raised palm replace the old horns and collar hand. Two hands total; full asymmetric butterfly cloak with two continuous long leaf-tipped tails; complete boots visible.
